0.0.n: Shortened まあ, used to ease into the statement.

0.2.n: Refers to a proposed law, not one already enacted.

0.3.n: Links 法案 to 中身, showing whose contents are being discussed.

0.4.n: Refers to the substance of the proposed law.

0.5.n: Marks 中身 as what the speaker would question.

0.6.n: The く form of 詳しい describes how the questioning would be done.

0.7.n: Plain form of a formal verb for asking about or examining something.

0.8.n: Links the preceding action to こと, presenting it as an idea.

0.9.n: Turns the preceding description into something that can be discussed as a whole.

0.10.n: Part of ではなくて, which rejects one description before moving to another.

0.11.n: Adds contrast within ではなくて; it is not translated separately here.

0.12.n: The connecting form of ない lets the sentence continue to what the speaker actually wants.

1.0.n: Adds emphasis to the speaker's polite request.

1.1.n: A title used here to address the listener, not a personal name.

1.2.n: Links 総理 to お考え, identifying whose thinking is meant.

1.3.n: The prefix お shows respect for the Prime Minister's views.

1.4.n: Links お考え to 元, identifying what has this foundation.

1.5.n: Refers to the underlying source or foundation of the Prime Minister's thinking.

1.6.n: Pairs with なる to identify the role something serves.

1.7.n: 元となる describes what forms the foundation, rather than necessarily indicating a change.

1.8.n: Refers abstractly to what underlies the thinking, not to a physical location.

1.9.n: Marks the underlying aspects as what the Prime Minister is asked to explain.

1.11.n: 分かる plus やすい means easy to understand; the く ending makes it describe the explanation.

1.12.n: The お plus verb-stem pattern joins いただく to respectfully request the listener's action.

1.13.n: Humbly presents the listener's explanation as a favor received by the speaker.

1.14.n: Introduces the condition that would make things helpful for the speaker.

1.15.n: Polite form of 助かる, used here to frame a request as something helpful.

2.0.n: A neutral first-person pronoun appropriate in this formal setting.

2.1.n: Marks 私 as the topic of the explanation.

2.2.n: あがり症 describes nervousness before others; な connects it to the explanatory もん.

2.3.n: Casual form of もの; with ですから, it introduces a personal explanation or excuse.

2.4.n: Adds politeness within the explanatory phrase もんですから.

2.5.n: Marks nervousness as the reason for reading from notes.

2.7.n: Refers to written prompts the speaker will read aloud.

2.8.n: Marks メモ as what is read; English naturally uses from here.

2.9.n: 読む becomes 読ませて plus いただきます, politely presenting reading as something the listener allows.

2.10.n: Softens the transition to asking forgiveness rather than expressing a strong contrast.

2.12.n: お plus the stem of 許す joins ください to make a respectful request.

2.13.n: Follows お許し to politely ask the listener to excuse the speaker.

2.14.n: Gently seeks the listener's understanding or agreement.

2.16.n: A brief acknowledgment that also signals readiness to continue.

3.0.n: Signals a transition from introductory remarks to the main discussion.

3.1.n: Refers to the central subject rather than preliminary remarks.

3.2.n: Marks 本論 as the destination of the figurative movement.

3.3.n: Polite form of 入る, used figuratively for beginning the main discussion.

0.lit: Well, not being a matter of questioning the bill's contents in detail,
0.tip: ということではなくて rejects one description and leads into what the speaker actually intends.

1.lit: By all means, if you explain understandably what forms the basis of the Prime Minister's thinking, it helps.
1.tip: お話しいただくと助かります makes a polite request by saying the listener's explanation would help.

2.lit: Because I am prone to stage fright, I will be allowed to read notes, but please forgive me, okay? Yes.
2.tip: 読ませていただきます humbly announces an action as something the listener permits.

3.lit: Now then, I will enter the main discussion.
3.tip: 本論に入ります is a standard formal way to announce that introductory remarks are finished.
